dimensions.name: Knowledge Delta
dimensions.justification: Adds concrete expert knowledge not usually known by a generic model: explicit break‑even formula for I/O‑Optimized (storage_GB × 0.4 M I/O), precise ACU cost ($0.12/ACU‑h), threshold rules (IO > 30% of bill, MinCapacity > 2 ACU with avg CPU < 10%), and detailed decision matrices for each cost lever. Some content merely restates AWS docs, preventing a perfect score.

dimensions.name: Mindset + Appropriate Procedures
dimensions.justification: Encodes AWS‑specific workflow: data‑gate validation, Cost Explorer reconciliation, CloudWatch & Performance Insights collection, ordered step‑by‑step dimension analysis, and precise CLI commands for each remediation. Only minor generic phrasing (e.g., “check data sufficiency”) prevents full marks.

dimensions.name: Anti-Pattern Quality
dimensions.justification: Provides an extensive NEVER list with concrete reasons (e.g., never switch I/O tier without break‑even calc, never drop Serverless MinCapacity below SLA, never buy RI for Serverless). Lacks a few edge‑case warnings (e.g., backtrack on low‑change workloads), so deduct one point.

dimensions.name: Specification Compliance
dimensions.justification: Full frontmatter, clear description, when_to_use/when_not_to_use, activation_triggers, invocation_schema, and a valid minimal invocation example. All required metadata present and well‑formed.

dimensions.name: Progressive Disclosure
dimensions.justification: Top‑level sections give a concise overview (what it does, decision tree) and deeper sections are deferred. However, the document is long and some details (e.g., full anti‑pattern list) are presented early, causing slight cognitive overload.

dimensions.name: Freedom Calibration
dimensions.justification: Destructive actions are tightly constrained (snapshot before change, CONFIRM gate, one‑dimension‑per‑window, batch size limit). Creative tasks (e.g., cost triage) are left freer. Minor over‑constraint on RI evaluation (no guidance on term selection) costs one point.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.justification: Follows a recognizable structure (Mindset → Process steps → Output contract → Anti‑patterns → Navigation). Minor ad‑hoc sections (e.g., quick start, expert heuristic) slightly break the pure pattern.

dimensions.name: Practical Usability
dimensions.justification: Provides actionable CLI snippets, savings formulas, and example output blocks. However, the output contract omits the NEED_MORE_INFO verdict that appears in the decision tree, creating a consistency gap. Some example blocks also omit optional sub‑fields, which could cause agent confusion. These issues reduce usability.
